tasks.title: Manifest TEU totals are short for 45-foot boxes
tasks.description: The vessel manifests we send to the line come out short on TEU whenever there are 45-foot high-cube boxes on board. The yard counts a 45 as two and a quarter TEU, like everyone else in the industry, but our totals treat it as a plain 40.
tasks.acceptance: teuOf counts a 45-foot container as two and a quarter TEU (20-foot and 40-foot boxes are unchanged), so a manifest of one 20-foot, one 40-foot and one 45-foot box totals five and a quarter TEU.

tasks.title: Port codes typed with a space or hyphen are not recognised
tasks.description: Agents copy port codes out of booking emails, where they are usually written with a space or a hyphen between the country and the location, and the lookup then says the port does not exist. Rotterdam written as NL RTM or nl-rtm should resolve exactly like NLRTM.
tasks.acceptance: normaliseLocode removes spaces and hyphens as well as normalising case, so normaliseLocode("nl-rtm") and normaliseLocode("NL RTM") both return "NLRTM" and portByCode("NL RTM") finds Rotterdam.

tasks.title: Berth fit ignores under-keel clearance
tasks.description: The berth planner offered a berth whose depth exactly matched the vessel's draft. Harbour rules require half a metre of under-keel clearance, so the vessel's draft plus that clearance has to be within the berth depth.
tasks.acceptance: fitsBerth requires the draft plus UNDER_KEEL_CLEARANCE_M to be within the berth depth: a vessel with a 14 m draft fits a berth 15 m deep, or exactly 14 m 50 cm deep, but not one 14 m deep or 14 m 40 cm deep. Length checks are unchanged.

tasks.title: Transit times are almost twice as long as they should be
tasks.description: Estimated arrivals are nearly a day late on longer legs. Distances are in nautical miles and speeds in knots, so the transit time is simply one divided by the other, but the estimate comes out about 85 percent too long.
tasks.acceptance: transitHours(240, 12) returns 20 and transitHours(90, 18) returns 5; arrivalTime uses the corrected transit time. distanceKm still converts nautical miles to kilometres.

tasks.title: Add Gdansk to the port registry
tasks.description: We start calling at the Baltic Hub in Gdansk next month and planners cannot select it. Please add it to the port registry: UN/LOCODE PLGDN, name Gdansk, country PL, time zone Europe/Warsaw, maximum draft 15 m, pilotage 2 hours.
tasks.acceptance: portByCode("PLGDN") returns Gdansk with country PL, timezone Europe/Warsaw, maxDraftM 15 and pilotageHours 2, and portsInCountry("PL") lists both PLGDN and PLGDY.

tasks.title: Feedermax vessel class is missing
tasks.description: The new regional loop uses Feedermax ships and the planner cannot size berths for them because the class is not in the vessel registry. Please add the class Feedermax: length 200 m, beam 30 m, draft 10 m, 3000 TEU.
tasks.acceptance: vesselClass("feedermax") returns a class named Feedermax with lengthM 200, beamM 30, draftM 10 and teu 3000.

tasks.title: Dangerous-goods check lets explosives sit next to oxidisers
tasks.description: A class 1 container was planned directly beside an oxidiser and the stowage check raised nothing. It looks like any hazard class written with a division, such as oxidisers or organic peroxides, is never matched against the segregation table.
tasks.acceptance: mustSegregate("1", "5.1"), mustSegregate("5.1", "1"), mustSegregate("2.1", "5.1") and mustSegregate("5.2", "3") are all true; mustSegregate("3", "8") and mustSegregate("8", "5.1") stay false; adjacentConflicts reports such pairs.

tasks.title: Back-to-back berth bookings are rejected
tasks.description: Planners cannot book a vessel onto a berth at the exact time the previous vessel leaves it. A booking that ends at noon and the next one starting at noon do not overlap, but the schedule reports a clash.
tasks.acceptance: The book method of BerthSchedule accepts a booking that starts exactly when another booking on the same berth ends (and one that ends exactly when another starts); bookings that genuinely overlap on the same berth are still refused.

tasks.title: Verified gross mass leaves out the container itself
tasks.description: The VGM figures we declare are lighter than the weighbridge readings by a couple of tonnes per box. Verified gross mass has to include the container's tare as well as the cargo; we only count the cargo.
tasks.acceptance: verifiedGrossMassTonnes returns cargo plus tare in tonnes: a box with 20000 kg of cargo and a 2200 kg tare has a VGM of 22200 kg (22 tonnes and 200 kg), and manifestWeightTonnes sums those values.

tasks.title: Arrival times are shown in UTC instead of port time
tasks.description: Customers in Singapore were told their vessel arrives at noon when it actually arrives in the evening local time. The arrival stamp is supposed to be in the destination port's own time zone from the registry.
tasks.acceptance: localArrival(new Date("2026-03-01T12:00:00Z"), "SGSIN") returns "2026-03-01 20:00" and for "NLRTM" returns "2026-03-01 13:00"; the format stays YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm and unknown ports are still rejected.

tasks.title: Rotterdam maximum draft is out of date
tasks.description: After this summer's dredging Rotterdam accepts deeper vessels, but the registry still has the old limit and the planner keeps turning ships away. The maximum draft for Rotterdam is now 24 m.
tasks.acceptance: portByCode("NLRTM") reports maxDraftM 24; every other Rotterdam field and every other port are unchanged.

tasks.title: Add the Neopanamax vessel class
tasks.description: Two Neopanamax ships join the transpacific service and the planner does not know the class. Please add Neopanamax to the vessel registry: length 366 m, beam 51 m, draft 15 m, 14000 TEU.
tasks.acceptance: vesselClass("Neopanamax") returns lengthM 366, beamM 51, draftM 15 and teu 14000; classesForPort includes it for Singapore and not for Gdynia.

decoys.title: Berth list flickers when two planners edit the same day
decoys.description: Duplicate of an earlier UI report; not reproducible in the planning service itself.

decoys.title: Antwerp pilotage hours disputed by the line
decoys.description: The line quoted a different pilotage estimate; the harbour authority confirmed the registry value is correct.

decoys.title: Reefer count includes empty reefers
decoys.description: Empty reefers are declared as reefers on purpose; working as intended.

decoys.title: Hamburg time zone shown as CET in summer
decoys.description: Reported against the old reporting tool, which is no longer used.

decoys.title: Planner allows booking of a berth under maintenance
decoys.description: Maintenance windows are now entered as bookings by the harbour master; no code change needed.

decoys.title: UN/LOCODE validation rejects codes with digits
decoys.description: Digits 2 to 9 are valid in the location part and are already accepted; the reporter used a zero.

decoys.title: ULCV draft value questioned
decoys.description: The registry holds the design draft for the class, not the scantling draft of individual ships.

decoys.title: Transit estimate ignores canal transits
decoys.description: Canal waiting times are handled by the voyage planning system, not by this service.

decoys.title: Segregation table missing class 9
decoys.description: Class 9 goods need no segregation from the classes we handle; no entry is required.

decoys.title: Manifest weight rounding differs from the weighbridge
decoys.description: Same root cause as another open cargo report.

decoys.title: Los Angeles shown with the wrong country
decoys.description: Fixed in the registry some time ago.

decoys.title: Post-Panamax beam listed incorrectly
decoys.description: Checked against class society data; the registry value is right.

decoys.title: Arrival time off by one minute
decoys.description: Arrival times are rounded to the millisecond and displayed to the minute; the difference is display only.

decoys.title: Berths with equal length sorted randomly
decoys.description: Candidate berths of equal length are now ordered by berth id.
